items.title: When R&D workforce expansion does not translate into innovation capability: evidence from Türkiye’s Technopark ecosystem
items.theme: Innovation systems, infrastructure and knowledge transfer
items.original_context: Abstract Many emerging economies use science, technology and innovation policy to expand R&D personnel, but larger research workforces do not necessarily generate stronger innovation capability. This article examines this problem through Türkiye as an illustrative emerging-economy case, where R&D personnel and researcher numbers have grown rapidly while selected innovation-output indicators continue to signal unresolved capability gaps. Drawing on comparative secondary indicators and semi-structured interviews with 38 managers and engineers in eight technoparks and two R&D centres, the study uses absorptive capacity to interpret why headcount

items.title: A new framework for industrial policy: the case of semiconductors in Japan and the United States
items.original_context: Abstract Interest in industrial policy has intensified in recent years, calling for renewed conceptual understanding and more robust analytical tools. However, existing industrial policy frameworks remain insufficient to capture the complexity and dynamics of contemporary industrial systems and policies. To address this gap, this study proposes a novel industrial policy analysis framework comprising four analytically distinct yet interrelated dimensions: drivers shaping policy, value-chain segments, product types, and policy instrument mixes.
